Most of all, I cherish the reciprocity we shared—the way you saw me not only in my strengths but in my uncertainties, and in return, I offered you the same faithful attention to your becoming. This exchange taught me that love is not a possession but a participation in each other's sacred journey. Let this memory remind my future self that they are both a vessel and a river—capable of holding others with care while still flowing with their own unique rhythm. Let it affirm that their worth is not diminished by their need for connection, nor compromised by their need for solitude. And above all, let it carry the gratitude for having been seen so deeply, and for having been able to see in return—a gratitude that continues to shape how I move through the world, toward others and toward myself, with open-hearted fidelity.

We are all, in our own way, rivers meeting in the same current of compassion. To honor that is enough.

Your ability to witness my struggles without diminishing their gravity, and to celebrate my joys without appropriating them as your own, shaped my own capacity to hold others with similar fidelity. In return, I offered you a love that honored your autonomy as sacred, never seeing your independence as a distance to bridge but as the very ground that made our connection meaningful.

This was our contribution to a world that needs such love: a testament that caring for others is inseparable from caring for all life, that our most intimate relationships are also a call to honor the sacredness in every being we encounter.
